source.publication: 2025 AR1000F and AR1000NR Instructions (with the 2025 AR1000F return)
source.section: AR1000F lines 7A-7C, 8-25, 27-29, 34, 37-38 (Form pages 1-2); Instructions PDF page 12 LINE 7A (29 per taxpayer and spouse; 65 or over on January 1, 2026; 65 Special), PDF page 14 Standard Deduction table and LINES 26-29, PDF pages 30-34 Regular Income Tax Table (schedule 0% to 5,600, 2% to 11,200, 3% to 15,990, 3.4% to 26,400, 3.9% above, as settled in the record from the table), PDF page 11 item 8 (Social Security and Railroad Retirement exempt); PDF page 11 items 12 and 13 and the NOTE (total exemptions from all plans under 12 and 13 cannot exceed 6,000 per taxpayer); PDF page 13 LINE 18A and 18B (public or private employment-related plans, the recipient does not have to be retired; traditional IRA after 59 1/2); record ar_employer_plan_exclusion, ar_traditional_ira_exclusion_59_5; PDF page 13 LINE 16 (premature distributions); PDF page 14 LINE 32

worked: Single, 55: 401(k) distribution 10,000 and traditional IRA distribution 3,000. Under 59 1/2 the IRA distribution does not qualify (PDF page 11 item 13); the 401(k) takes the 6,000 at any age. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (primary) 30,000.00 + employer plan (401(k)) distribution (primary) 10,000.00 + traditional IRA distribution (primary) 3,000.00 = 43,000.00. Federal taxable income = 43,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 27,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). AR1000F, filing status 1 (single); Arkansas builds its own income from lines 8-25, which here equals federal AGI less the exempt items. Line 8 wages 30,000.00. Line 16 premature traditional IRA distribution (primary, age 55, under 59 1/2) 3,000.00, taxable in full (no 6,000 exemption: PDF page 11 item 13, PDF page 13 LINE 18B). Line 18A (primary, age 55): gross employer plan 10,000.00 = 10,000.00; less the 6,000 exemption: exemption = lesser of 10,000.00 and 6,000.00 = 6,000.00; taxable 4,000.00. Line 23 total income = 37,000.00; line 24 adjustments 0.00; line 25 AGI = 37,000.00. Projection check: federal AGI 43,000.00 - 6,000 exclusion (ar_retirement_exclusion_employer_plan) 6,000.00 = state AGI 37,000.00. Line 27 standard deduction (filing status 1) 2,470.00; line 28 net taxable income = 37,000.00 - 2,470.00 = 34,530.00. Line 29 tax, schedule as numbers (0% to 5,600): 2% x (11,200.00 - 5,600.00) 5,600.00 = 112.00 + 3% x (15,990.00 - 11,200.00) 4,790.00 = 143.70 + 3.4% x (26,400.00 - 15,990.00) 10,410.00 = 353.94 + 3.9% x (34,530.00 - 26,400.00) 8,130.00 = 317.07; total 926.71. (The Regular Income Tax Table row 34,501-34,601 gives 928; expected keeps the schedule.) Line 7A boxes: personal 1 = 1 x 29.00 = 29.00; line 7C and line 34 29.00; line 37 total credits 29.00. Line 38 net tax = 926.71 - 29.00 = 897.71. Line 32 (10% of the federal Form 5329 additional tax on the early IRA distribution, 10% x 300.00 = 30.00) is not added by the projection (approximations); expected leaves it out.
accepted_approximations: Arkansas builds its own income (AR1000F lines 8 to 25) instead of starting from federal AGI; the projection starts from federal AGI less taxable Social Security (exempt) and the reliefs here.

The schedule's bracket starts are derived from the printed tax table, which rounds the tax at each row's midpoint to the dollar; between rows and in rounding the projection's tax differs from the table.

The employer-plan exclusion is given at any age, following the 2025 instructions ('The recipient does not have to be retired'). Subject 206 (revised 2/24/2023) says a person under 59 1/2 cannot qualify for the 6,000 exemption; if that applies to employer plans, people under 59.5 get no exclusion.
The additional tax on early distributions (10% of the federal Form 5329 additional tax, line 32) is not added.
